correctness.rationale: An independent subset of the crown graph is a subset of one shore or the two matched vertices at one index, giving W(u,v)=N1_(u=0)+N1_(v=0)+n-1-2|u+v|. Odd n zeros are u,v !=0 with |u+v|=(n-1)/2, each shell vector has N-2 allowed ordered choices, while even n has no zero. The exact zero-shell Fourier inverse produces Krawtchouk kernel q(x,y), and averaging ANY projection over translations yields the unique Fourier-diagonal range projector of no larger l1/linfty norm, hence sharpness. Splitting kernel mass at origin/diagonal/off-diagonal gives Lambda_n=1+[D+(N-4)L-2(N-2)B]/N²; Krawtchouk generating function yields L=2^((n+1)/2)B; Jensen/triangle show Theta growth. Independent integer Walsh and inverse-kernel computations check n=3,5: 18/300 zero frequencies and norms 49/16,733/128.

value.rationale: The parity contrast between an invertible Boolean convolution and a growing projection norm even as odd-size nullity fraction vanishes is mathematically motivated and relevant for Fourier recovery and finite combinatorial harmonic analysis. All-length sharp growth is a nontrivial structural consequence, not just a small-graph enumeration.

final_claim: For crown H_n=K_(n,n) minus perfect matching (n>=3), the independent-set convolution multiplier has an explicit Walsh formula; even n are invertible, odd n have a binomial Hamming-shell nullspace and sharp globally minimal endpoint range-projection norm with growth Theta(2^(n/2)/sqrt(n)).
limitations: Specific to K_n,n with perfect matching removed, n>=3, complex/real endpoint l1/linfty; leading asymptotic constant not determined, only Theta order.
